artifacts.description: Package entry: name, one-line purpose, canonical command, role list
Primary agent instructions: role, responsibilities, steps, output contract
Package manifest: permissions, memory policy, read allow/deny lists
Fail-closed build readiness profile; only a complete user-confirmed minimal-private receipt can opt out of quality dossiers
Identity card: name, slug, summary, verb_object capabilities, entrypoints
Routing card: >=6 triggers (>=3 ko, >=3 en), >=4 anti-triggers (>=2 ko, >=2 en), semantic workforce block, risk profile, entrypoints, memory behavior — no card, no auto-routing

A2A (Agent2Agent v1.0.1) Agent Card, projected from .agentlas/agent-card.json + .agentlas/routing-card.json by package_contract.write_a2a_projection() on every scaffold/verify — never hand-authored (owner decision 2026-08-08, R1: a second identity file drifts from the real one). url anchors on the immutable agentId (R5), not the mutable slug. Team mode projects one card for the whole team (the orchestrator entrypoint), not one per worker.
Memory ownership map
Per-runtime slash command adapters
MCP tool allowlist and resolution order
Skill registry (empty list allowed)
Append-only candidate memory events ledger (empty on export); every builder emits it and the team gate rejects a package without it
Positive/negative eval prompts with pass criteria
Interview-derived work brief: goal, constraints, decisions

>=10 routing benchmark cases (route + reject, ko + en), generated from the package routing card instead of copied from an internal fixture. Canonical path is the plural `.agentlas/routing-benchmarks.jsonl`, which is what 140 of 144 forge packages and 183 live Hub releases actually ship. The contract previously said `benchmarks/`, which no generation ever wrote, so every package failed this required artifact on the path alone while the file sat on disk. The spelling carries no meaning; only agreement does.
Interview summary that grounded this package
Sources consulted during build research
Selected and rejected tools/plugins, permission boundaries, fallbacks, and smoke tests
Interview, comparable-agent, theory, and tool findings synthesized into specialist behavior
Performance-oriented prompt contract with operating loop, examples, rubric, and refusal rules

Worker roster: one folder per worker at agents/<role>/agent.md, plus an orchestrator/HQ and a company-blueprint topology that names them — a team with zero workers is not a team. Verified by the same team-shape rule scripts/verify-team-package.sh runs
Team topology: orchestrator, nodes, edges
Task flow: produces/consumes graph

INPUT contract: the JSON Schema for what a requester must hand over before this method can start. Direction is carried by the filename because no package ever marked it any other way, and a schema whose direction has to be guessed from its title cannot be matched against a request. Every stated need becomes a property; `required` names the ones without which the work does not begin. Any enum reachable from matching MUST carry an escape member ("other", "unknown") - a closed list is how one stated requirement took a 3-candidate inventory to 0.

OUTPUT contract: the JSON Schema for what the requester ends up holding. The brief compiler reads only this file's TOPOLOGY - arity and value spaces - to derive shape, rowVerdict and verdictValues, so nothing here depends on the words the author chose. Extra domain schemas may sit beside it; this is the one the matcher reads.

One real instance of output.schema.json. The publish gate validates it with a JSON Schema validator, never with a model - under BYOM the only honest defence against marking your own homework is that the marker is not a model.

Tool/MCP requirement declaration, projected from .agentlas/mcp-policy.json + agentlas.json by package_contract.project_tools_requirements() on every verify — never hand-authored (edit mcp-policy.json instead). Body is YAML-compatible JSON; PyYAML is not a dependency anywhere in this codebase.
Shell/network/file/payment permission whitelist, projected from agentlas.json's toolPermissions/allowRead/denyRead — never hand-authored (edit agentlas.json instead).

Declares (never implements) the memory-ticket/self-evolution lifecycle this package expects, projected from .agentlas/memory-map.json. Enforcement stays with the OS-resident memory curator (owner decision 2026-08-08, #9) — this file never carries policy or judge logic.
Declares (never implements) session-end cleanup/reporting expectations, projected from agentlas.json. The host Stop hook performs the actual flush.

Authorship/license/mint-time record. Minted ONCE at first build from agentlas.json + .agentlas/agent-card.json and preserved verbatim afterwards, the same mint-once rule as agentId (R5) — component changes bump the package version, never this file. Optional (not required=true): it depends on agentId, which is minted by the upload wizard, not by a bare scaffold/verify — a package that has never been through run_setup_wizard legitimately has no provenance.json yet.

Points to the agent-level eval surface. The actual data stays at .agentlas/capability-eval-plan.json and .agentlas/routing-benchmarks.jsonl — moving it to evals/ was tried once (the contract's own routing-benchmarks.jsonl description records it) and broke every package that generation never followed, so this folder documents the split instead of duplicating the data.
Sealed-chip-only rules for this folder (Secret-Free DTO, no raw memory). Actual chips are written here by the experience pipeline at runtime, not by the builder.
RAG source-file drop point (optional per the plan's own [선택] tag). Empty is a valid, common state.

Optional (plan's own [선택] tag). Points to contracts/intake.schema.json + output.schema.json, which already carry this package's JSON Schemas — this folder exists only for agents with fixed multimodal I/O shapes beyond those two.
Optional (plan's own [선택] tag). Execution-isolation defaults, conservative by default (no network, no shell) — widen explicitly per package if the agent needs more.
Optional (plan's own [선택] tag). Points to contracts/output.example.json, this package's one publish-validated example.

The compiled resume, schemaVersion agentlas.brief/1, side=offer. Written by the upload path so an author can read exactly what the routing layer sees, and NOT shipped: every field is derived from the card, the manifest and contracts/ that travel with it, so including it would tie the package's identity to the compiler — improving how a shape is inferred would mint a new release for every published package without one of them having changed. The reader compiles its own from the same sources.
